The structure of LiNbF₅ crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Cmcm (No. 63), with a unit cell containing 28 atoms—Li₄Nb₄F₂₀—distributed over five independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Li and Nb each coordinated by six F neighbors, while F centers adopt square-pyramidal and four-coordinate environments. Validated polyhedron-sharing analysis identifies corner-sharing between square-pyramidal F polyhedra and between four-vertex F polyhedra, with additional corner-sharing between Li- and Nb-centered six-vertex polyhedra. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component spanning all 28 sites.
